source_backed_facts.fact: William D. Menor established the homestead beside the Snake River in the 1890s and built the cabin incrementally.
NPS identifies a west wing built in 1894 and a central section added around 1895.
The west wing served as bedroom and sitting room, while the central section housed the kitchen and pantry.
The building used local timber and lime whitewash; NPS specifically identifies rough-sawn boards in the central section.
HABS records restoration of the homestead cabin and attached store in 1949.
source_backed_facts.note: Use HABS drawings and current official references to separate historic form from later restoration work.

source_backed_facts.fact: Bill Menor attached the store building to the east end of his homestead cabin.
NPS identifies the larger east wing as built around 1905 and used as the general store.
The store served settlers and travelers and also supported Menor's post-office and ferry business.
The country-store wing is part of the Homestead footprint and is not the nearby Storehouse used for protected food and root crops.
